newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan March trade surplus down 37.3 percent yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan March trade surplus down 37.3 percent yr/yr.

text.p: Taiwan had a trade surplus of US$555 million in March, down 37.3 percent compared to US$885 million in March 1996, the finance ministry said on Tuesday.
Taiwan's exports in March totalled US$10.67 billion, a rise of 18.4 percent from March 1996, the ministry said.
Imports rose an annual 24.5 percent to US$10.11 billion -- which the ministry noted was the first time Taiwan's monthly imports had surpassed US$10 billion.
The March surplus was very close to the expectations of Taiwan economists as reflected in an April 3 Reuters Poll.
The Reuters Poll yielded an average forecast for US$590 million surplus or a year-on-year decline of 33.3 percent.
The March export and import figures both were somewhat higher than the economists' respective average forecasts of US$9.672 billion and US$9.082 billion.

Hsu said a pork export ban ordered on March 20 due to an islandwide outbreak of highly contagious hog foot and mouth disease did not affect Taiwan's export total for March, which was the second highest monthly figure ever.
The pork crisis is sure to hit exports from April, he said.
Noting that 1996 pork exports were US$1.55 billion, Hsu said the ban likely would slash Taiwan's total exports by an average US$130 million per month through the rest of 1997.
The ministry said the export growth in March was due mainly to a global economic expansion, adding that the expansion should continue to fuel Taiwan's exports in the coming months.

March exports to the United States rose 26.8 percent to US$2.477 billion from US$1.953 billion in March 1996. Hong Kong was the next biggest destination with exports totalling US$2.426 billion, up 16.8 percent from US$2.078 billion in March 1996.

Japan remained Taiwan's top import source, accounting for US$2.529 billion or 25 percent of the total, followed by Europe at US$2.156 billion (21.3 percent) and the United States at US$2.026 billion (20 percent).
The March trade surplus with Hong Kong, which serves as the main conduit for Taiwan's lucrative and growing trade with rival China, remained the largest by far at US$2.261 billion.
Taiwan's trade deficit with Japan was US$1.383 billion, up 13.5 percent from a year earlier.
-- Taipei Newsroom (5080815)
